_comment: I0 provider playbook (schema: app/domain/playbook.py). Public facts only, every claim sourced. Binance (.com) and Binance.US (BAM Trading Services, a separate company with no Binance records) are two entities. The Kodex portals and the Binance.US LERT inbox are LE-only: a victim / PI / counsel goes to Binance Customer Service (support chat), which escalates to the legal team. The current stolen-funds FAQ says Binance cannot freeze without an official freezing order: no courtesy freeze and no police-report clock are modelled.
notes: Binance (.com) lists no instrument by jurisdiction: it discloses 'as legally required' and needs an official freezing order from law enforcement or a court of competent jurisdiction. Binance.US acts on US law enforcement and government agencies only (official government e-mail domains). The LE e-mail addresses Binance publishes (Binance.US LERT; a Russia / Belarus LE inbox on a sibling domain) are not catalogued: their local parts are not on the reviewed alias list, and they are LE-only anyway.

entities.name: BAM Trading Services Inc. (Binance.US)
entities.notes: Separate company: it has no records for Binance and cannot answer requests addressed to Binance. Binance.US Web3 wallet requests go separately to BAM Technology Services Inc.

sibling.purpose: Binance.US (BAM Trading): its LERT inbox for US law enforcement and its support site
Law-enforcement inbox for Russia and Belarus named in the stolen-funds FAQ (Binance left Russia in 2023: confirm before relying on it)

channels.label: Government Law Enforcement Request System (Kodex)
channels.notes: For government and law enforcement agencies only. Works only in Chrome or Edge; agency verification over a VPN is not completed. Mark urgent cases 'Exigent' (processed immediately). Aegis never registers or submits there: the officer does, with the pack.

channels.label: Law Enforcement Request System, mainland China (Kodex)
Law-enforcement inbox for Russia and Belarus
channels.notes: The stolen-funds FAQ names an inbox on the binanceholdings.ru domain for Russian and Belarusian law enforcement. Not catalogued (local part not on the reviewed alias list); medium confidence since Binance left Russia in 2023.

channels.label: Binance Customer Service (support chat)
channels.notes: Where the stolen-funds FAQ sends victims, and where the privacy portal sends legal representatives with court-order freezing or disclosure requests (escalated to the legal team). Non-users continue in the chat as a Visitor. Customer Service will not share law-enforcement case details.

channels.label: Binance.US Law Enforcement Response Team (LERT)
channels.notes: The LERT inbox on the binance.us domain (published in the Binance.US LE guide). Answers only official law-enforcement or government e-mail domains; US agencies. Not catalogued (local part not on the reviewed alias list).

channels.label: Binance.US support team
channels.notes: The LE guide sends scam victims to the Binance.US support team and / or IC3; it gives no separate victim process. Confirm the support URL before use.

binance.le.notes: Binance's LE channel is the Kodex request system (binance.kodex; mainland China: binance.kodex_cn), for government and law enforcement agencies only.

instrument.notes: No instrument opens the ticket; the FAQ asks for a copy of the police report.

paths.conflict: Older mirrored or localised versions of the FAQ (unsourced: reported, not linked here) describe a discretionary 'temporary courtesy freeze' and a police-report deadline (24 hours, later 7 days). The canonical page (published 2018, no update date) has neither: no clock is set, and a hold is never assumed.
paths.notes: Binance says it is 'unable to unilaterally freeze any user's assets without an appropriate official freezing order' from law enforcement or a court; it liaises with law enforcement directly and updates come from the officer. Value: Binance is told while the funds sit, and the ticket goes into the officer's Kodex request. Hand off to LE as soon as the ticket arrives.

instrument.notes: A court order behind a freezing or disclosure request; the page names no court or jurisdiction.

paths.notes: The one documented route for a legal representative: Customer Service escalates court-order freezing / disclosure requests to the legal team. Which courts Binance accepts is not stated.

instrument.notes: An 'appropriate official freezing order' from law enforcement or a court of competent jurisdiction; disclosure 'as legally required'. Mark emergencies 'Exigent' as the legal process type.

paths.conflict: A DOJ memo reported in Jul 2026 said Binance would end courtesy freezes and require MLAT or formal process; Binance publicly denied any change (reported only, low confidence). Public reporting also describes partial or slow freezes in some cases.
paths.notes: Exigent cases are 'processed immediately'; no other SLA is published. The officer registers on Kodex with an official agency e-mail.

instrument.notes: The guide also points victims to IC3.

paths.notes: Freezes and records are for US law enforcement only: file IC3 and hand off to the case officer.

instrument.notes: A formal freeze request from an official government e-mail domain, supported by probable cause that the funds are subject to seizure and forfeiture; name, position and direct contact of the requesting official.

deadlines.action: LERT may freeze the account for two weeks: serve a seizure warrant or court order before it lapses (follow-up inferred).

paths.notes: Binance.US answers US law enforcement and government agencies (documented). Inferred, not stated by Binance.US: a non-US agency goes through a US agency or an MLAT.

instrument.notes: Grand jury subpoena, court order, search warrant or seizure warrant (requirements vary by jurisdiction).

paths.notes: Users are not told of government requests. A 'no records' confirmation comes back when nothing is found. Urgent productions are attempted, with no guaranteed time frame.
Seizure warrants are listed as valid legal process; the forfeiture route that follows (18 USC 981 / 982) is inferred.

reply_signals.phrase: For Government and Law Enforcement Agencies only
escalate your case to the legal team
